So, what D is saying about core society is that our society is first and foremost anti-love. It does not allow for people to love each other. For example, in school, without school, your parents would just care about your happiness. But because of school, they care about your grades and whether or not you get into an elite American college and whether or not you get a good job. As a result, the parents deny your free will, deny your agency, and you don't feel loved.

Right? In a normal relationship, your parents would just let you do whatever you want. But because they think if I let you do whatever you want, you will not do well in school and won’t be able to get a job, then you'll become unemployed or a drug addict. That’s how they think. Mhm. Does that make sense? Yeah. So the denial of free will is anti-love and therefore it's evil because it limits you from getting closer to Monad.

Just like Amber mentions that this world is anti-love, but what is the purpose of not letting us get closer to the Monad? That’s a good question. Why are they doing this? Because the people in power want to stay in power. They gain benefits such as power by disobeying the Monad and letting others do the same because it allows them to coordinate well together. So, different people will interpret this model differently.

In their conception, the Monad is the evil one, and their god is the good one. They're liberating us from the Monad by making us more focused on the material world. But the reality is that they got their power because of a religion promoting transgression which allowed them to coordinate well together. Now that they have this power, they need to rationalize why they have it and develop systems to maintain it. That's why we live in this world today.

They want to maintain power, so they will think of new ideas that allow them to keep this power even if it means denying the truth. This is a theory—no one knows if it’s true or not. But nomad does not have two meanings; it has one with different names but one meaning. The nomad is the divine son, the source of all life.

Plato defines nomad as knowledge, and Dante defines it as love. For Plato, the pursuit of knowledge allows you to get closer to the Monad. For Dante, it’s a pursuit of love. This is the perfect, immutable, eternal. What Plato and Dante are debating is how to return to the Monad: through knowledge or love.

This is similar to Buddhism, which is exactly about the ultimate end of things in a more spiritual aspect, not something physical that we can interpret as one thing or another. So this is really interesting how different religious traditions have the same conception of the world and universe.
